::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to use LaTeX on blogspot?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/13865/how-to-use-latex-on-blogspot), asked by [roxrook](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4322/roxrook) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-19; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I'm trying to use LaTeX on my blog, but I could not figure out how. Has anyone done it before? Any feedback or related information would be greatly appreciated.
:::

I would say use [MathJax](http://www.mathjax.org/).  It's a AJAX engine for LaTeX syntax that now is distributed by a CDN so you don't have to upload a single file to your blogspot account.

To enable MathJax, just drop in

```html
<script type="text/javascript" src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.1/latest/MathJax.js">
MathJax.Hub.Config({
 extensions: ["tex2jax.js","TeX/AMSmath.js","TeX/AMSsymbols.js"],
 jax: ["input/TeX", "output/HTML-CSS"],
 tex2jax: {
     inlineMath: [ ['$','$'], ["\\(","\\)"] ],
     displayMath: [ ['$$','$$'], ["\\[","\\]"] ],
 },
 "HTML-CSS": { availableFonts: ["TeX"] }
});
</script>
```

after the header (`<head>`) in the Blogger template (Design→Edit HTML→Edit Template). 

Googling "install mathjax blogspot" led me to a page on the Web Applications StackExchange: [MathJax on Blogger](https://webapps.stackexchange.com/questions/13053/mathjax-on-blogger).

See the MathJax pages for more information about configuring and using it.
